s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis and is being treated with fluconazole, which may increase the risk of lymphoma

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, hypotension, and rash, which are common symptoms of this disease

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a new skin eruption and is immunocompromised, which may increase the risk of this disease

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is a key diagnostic feature of intravascular lymphoma. This finding, combined with the patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and a new widespread skin eruption, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While cutaneous T-cell lymphoma can present with skin eruptions, the specific finding of intravascular atypical cells on biopsy is more characteristic of intravascular lymphoma.

rejected.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma often presents with nasal or upper respiratory tract involvement, which is not mentioned in the case vignette.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma typically presents with systemic symptoms such as fever, night sweats, and weight loss, but the biopsy findings do not specifically support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
rejected.why: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is often associated with HTLV-1 infection and has distinct clinical and pathological features that are not described in the case vignette.
